q: Does switching between Afghan, imported and local coal change a Pakistani cement plant's CO2?
title: Coal source and CO2 at Pakistani plants
short: Per unit of heat the difference is modest, since most bituminous and subbituminous coals sit near 95 kg CO2 per GJ; per tonne it can be large, because heat content varies. Work out CO2 from each lot's tonnes and lab tested heat value or carbon content, not from a single factor per tonne.
audience: Cement plants in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa buying coal from several sources

p: A tonne of high ash local coal and a tonne of imported coal give very different heat. A per tonne factor overstates one and understates the other.

ul: Tonnes per lot from weighbridge and invoices.
Lab gross calorific value, ash and moisture per lot.

p: Thar lignite has a higher CO2 per GJ than bituminous coal. Treat it as its own fuel.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, raw material and electricity invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per plant, so the clinker and cement figures can be traced back to the documents behind them.
